definition: A fear day is a day when SPY fell more than 1.5%, or the fear gauge (the VIX) rose more than 15% in a day, closed at 25 or higher, or closed at 20 or higher on a day when SPY or QQQ fell.

explanation.body: Its current reading is from 2026-10-30. Its study record, the history it was built and checked on, holds 3 counted items on file. Nothing from the record on file is missing. The next update arrives at the next session close on this page's normal schedule.
explanation.summary: Show what the record actually says followed fear days, and keep a forward record of each new fear day so it can be graded.

qualified_by: the fear gauge rose more than 15% that day

proving_note: Still being proven: the ranking below rests on a finished study, but this page's own forward record has not started yet, so nothing it could say about the next fear day has been graded.

study.fear_day_meaning: In that study, a fear day meant SPY fell at least 1% in a day, or SPY closed below its average of the last 50 sessions. That is not the same as the definition at the top of this page.
study.mechanism: On fear days, rising-trend stocks are ranked by how deep their dip is compared with that same stock's own past dips.
study.setting: Rising-trend names on fear days, each name's move measured against the same day's average move
study.spread_words: top fifth against bottom fifth, 2023 onward
